subject: Week 1: In the beginning. Genesis and Exodus.
body:
Good morning.

Welcome to the Old Testament in three months. This week is creation, the flood, Abraham, Jacob, Joseph, and the escape from Egypt. Ten chapters a day, and almost all of it is story.

Do not stop to study every detail. Just read and let it pull you in. This is the foundation everything else stands on.

Your dashboard has each day's chapters. I am reading with you.

Heather

subject: Week 2: The wilderness years
body:
Good morning.

This week you finish Exodus, walk through Leviticus, and get deep into Numbers. I will be honest: this is the stretch where people quit. All the laws and offerings can feel like a manual for a world that is gone.

Here is what to hold onto. Every rule exists because God wanted to live among His people. The whole section is Him saying, I want to be close, and here is how.

Push through. If you are still reading at the end of this week, you can finish the whole thing.

Heather

subject: Week 3: Moses says goodbye, Joshua steps up
body:
Good morning.

Big week. Moses gives his farewell speech in Deuteronomy, Joshua leads the people into the land, and Judges begins the long spiral of forgetting God and finding Him again.

Watch for one word over and over in Deuteronomy: remember. Moses knew what happens to people who forget what God has done. So do we.

Heather

subject: Week 4: Judges, Ruth, and a shepherd king
body:
Good morning.

This week has some of the best stories in the whole Bible. Gideon and Samson, Ruth's quiet faithfulness, Samuel hearing God's voice as a boy, David and Goliath, and David's rise and fall.

Notice that the Bible never cleans anyone up. David at his best and David at his worst are both on the page. That honesty is one of the reasons you can trust this book.

Heather

subject: Week 5: Kings, temples, and a divided house
body:
Good morning.

Solomon builds the temple this week, the kingdom splits in two, and Elijah stands alone against the prophets of Baal. Then Chronicles begins retelling the story with different eyes.

When you hit the name lists in Chronicles, do not stall out. Read them like a memorial wall, every name was a real person in God's story, and keep moving.

Heather

subject: Week 6: Exile and the long road home
body:
Good morning.

This week the kingdom falls, the temple burns, and the people are carried to Babylon. Then, seventy years later, they come home. Ezra rebuilds the temple, Nehemiah rebuilds the wall, and Esther risks her life for her people.

It is heavy reading and hopeful reading in the same week. Broken things get rebuilt. That is the whole point.

Heather

subject: Week 7: Job and the songs begin
body:
Good morning.

Job asks the hardest question in the Bible this week: why do good people suffer? And God answers, not with an explanation, but with Himself. Sometimes we do not get to know why. We get to know who.

Then the Psalms begin. Read them out loud when you can. They were written to be spoken.

Heather

subject: Week 8: Deep in the Psalms
body:
Good morning.

A whole week inside the Psalms. Crying out, praising, doubting, trusting, all of it mixed together, which is exactly what a real life with God looks like.

If one psalm grabs you this week, stop and read it twice. This is the one part of the plan where lingering is the point.

You are past halfway. I am proud of you.

Heather

subject: Week 9: Wisdom for ordinary days
body:
Good morning.

You finish the Psalms this week and walk into Proverbs, wisdom for money, words, work, friendship, and family. It is the most practical stretch of the whole Old Testament.

Try this: each day, pick one proverb and carry it around. Say it at dinner. Wisdom sticks when it gets used the same day.

Heather

subject: Week 10: Ecclesiastes, the Song, and Isaiah begins
body:
Good morning.

Ecclesiastes is the most honest book in the Bible, life without God is vapor, and it is not afraid to say so. The Song of Solomon celebrates love without blushing. And then Isaiah opens: judgment is coming, but so is a child, a servant, a King.

For unto us a child is born. You will read those words this week, written seven hundred years before Bethlehem.

Heather

subject: Week 11: Comfort, and a weeping prophet
body:
Good morning.

Isaiah 53 is this week. Read it slowly. He was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities. It is the clearest picture of Jesus in the whole Old Testament.

Then Jeremiah, who preached his whole life to people who would not listen and kept going anyway. Faithfulness does not always look like success. Sometimes it just looks like showing up.

Heather

subject: Week 12: Ruins, visions, and dry bones
body:
Good morning.

Lamentations sits in the ruins of Jerusalem and still says: great is His faithfulness, His mercies are new every morning. That verse was not written on a good day. That is what makes it strong enough to hold you on a bad one.

Then Ezekiel's valley of dry bones, Daniel in the lions' den, and the beginning of the twelve small prophets. One week left.

Heather

subject: Week 13: The last word, and then silence
body:
Good morning.

This is your last week. Twelve short prophets, each with one urgent thing to say. Micah tells you what God requires: do justice, love mercy, walk humbly. Habakkuk decides to rejoice even if everything fails. Malachi gets the last word, and then four hundred years of silence, waiting for a voice in the wilderness.

You read the entire Old Testament in three months. Very few people ever do that. When you finish, your certificate is waiting on your dashboard.

I am so proud of you. Thank you for reading alongside me.

With love,
Heather
